title: Catching the Wind
logline: On a windy stretch of the southern coast, kite makers fight to get a huge kite airborne, and then, for a few minutes, barely touch the line at all.
human_question: What is the difference between wanting to make something fly and wanting it to be seen flying?

premise.story: A day among kite makers building and flying large kites in the windy season: the hard, repeated struggle of the launch, the sudden ease once a kite catches the wind, rivalries between makers, and the pride and disappointment of a day's flying.
premise.place: A beach or open field on the southern coast during the kite-flying season.
premise.experience: Wind, fabric and bamboo; the strain of the launch giving way to a long, steady glide; small figures on the ground craning upward.

concept_links.why: This is close to the concept's own image: an effortful start that gives way to a settled, steady holding, and the wish to do something well that is not the same as clinging to how it looks to others [C021-P:L33] [C021-P:L41] [C021-M:L27].

A kite launched easily on a good day and one wrestled up against a difficult wind echo the concept's account of conditions, such as weather, that favour spontaneous over effortful arising [C006-P:L46-L52].

what_camera_could_observe: The struggle of launching into the wind
A kite settling and gliding with only small corrections
Rival makers watching each other's kites
The maker's face at the moment a kite finally holds
what_must_be_real: The makers' actual rivalry, skill and disappointments. No wind or outcome staged.

possible_arc.opening: Bamboo frames and fabric laid out on sand.
possible_arc.turn: A difficult launch, again and again, until the kite catches.
possible_arc.ending_open: The kite holds, falls, or is outflown by a rival. Reality decides.

requirements: An open beach or field with reliable seasonal wind
Kite makers willing to be filmed over more than one flying day
Good long-lens and wide coverage for kites at height

suggestions.name: A beach near Tangalle or Mirissa during the kite season
suggestions.why: The south coast has open beaches and a seasonal kite-flying tradition.
suggestions.season_notes: Kite-flying season is typically February to March.
suggestions.verify: No kite maker has been contacted; the season and general tradition are plausible but the specific group is unconfirmed.

risks: Being a merely pretty metaphor without real stakes
Rivalry between makers escalating beyond what consent covers
drop_if: No maker or rivalry with a real stake can be found and filmed over a full flying day

connections.note: Two open-air disciplines built on repeated effort, one chasing wind, one chasing a place on a team.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
